question: A group of scientists is conducting an experiment on the human cells involved in the immune response. They genetically modify B cells so they do not express the cluster of differentiation 21 (CD21) on their cell surfaces. The pathogenesis of which of the following organisms would most likely be affected by this genetic modification?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "CD21 on B cells" -> "important for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) entry" -> "EBV pathogenesis affected" -> 95% CHAIN: "CD21 on B cells" -> "important for Measles virus entry" -> "Measles virus pathogenesis affected" -> 90% CHAIN: "CD21 on B cells" -> "not directly involved in HIV pathogenesis" -> "HIV pathogenesis not affected" -> 80% CHAIN: "CD21 on B cells" -> "not directly involved in Human papillomavirus pathogenesis" -> "HPV pathogenesis not affected" -> 80% CHAIN: "CD21 on B cells" -> "not directly involved in Parvovirus B19 pathogenesis" -> "Parvovirus B19 pathogenesis not affected" -> 95%
analysis: CD21, also known as complement receptor 2 (CR2), plays a crucial role in the activation and regulation of B cells. It acts as a receptor for the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), allowing the virus to enter and infect B cells. Therefore, genetic modification of B cells to not express CD21 would most likely affect the pathogenesis of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).
